findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data; @updatedAt is not bumped
findings.body: The new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is preceded by the comment `// Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential`, but the `data` argument is an empty object. Prisma does not update any column (including `@updatedAt`) when `data` is empty, so this is effectively a no-op (or, depending on the Prisma version, throws) while pretending to refresh the timestamp. Either remove the call (the author notes the webhook handler already updates this field) or pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` so the intent matches the behavior.

findings.title: deleteCache success path does not invalidate connectedCalendars; UI stays stale
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only fires `onSuccess?.()` on success. The companion `disconnectMutation` immediately below (lines 53-65) explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` via `onSettled`. After the user clicks "Delete cached data", the `CalendarCache` rows are deleted server-side but `connectedCalendar.cacheUpdatedAt` in cache keeps showing the old value, so the dropdown keeps displaying the same `Last updated: ...` line and the destructive action appears to have done nothing. Add the same `async onSettled` invalidation block (or an `onSuccess`-side invalidate) to `deleteCacheMutation` so the UI reflects deletion.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt))` ignores the user's locale and uses month/day/year, which is incorrect and confusing for users on non-en-US locales (e.g., users with `de`, `fr`, `ja`). Use the locale-aware helper exposed by `useLocale`/i18n (e.g., `formatInTimeZone` from `date-fns-tz` or `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale)`) so the display matches the rest of the app.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, returns expired caches
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all rows for the credential and returns the max `updatedAt` regardless of `expiresAt`. Cache rows live for `CACHING_TIME = ONE_MONTH_IN_MS`; once they all expire, this still returns the last write timestamp and the dropdown will keep displaying `Last updated: <30+ days ago>` even though no live cache exists. Filter the `groupBy` with `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or join/max only non-expired rows) so the UI only shows status for currently valid cache entries.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without declaring tsx
findings.body: The script changes from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` is not declared in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`, while `ts-node` is still a devDependency (line 196) and is still used by `check-changed-files` and `translate-locales` (lines 24-25). Either add `"tsx": "..."` to devDependencies (preferred) so the version is pinned, or revert to `ts-node` for consistency. Relying on `npx` to fetch `tsx` on demand risks version drift, slower startup, and silent failures in offline/CI environments.

findings.title: macOS-only sed -i '' syntax breaks on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses BSD/macOS in-place edit syntax. On GNU sed (Linux) `-i` requires an extension argument, so this either errors or creates a literal backup file named `''`. Detect the platform (e.g., `[[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]] && sed -i '' ... || sed -i ...`) or use a portable approach (perl in-place, or write to a temp file and rename) so the script works for non-macOS developers and CI runners.

findings.title: Prisma warning contradicts the actual SQL (default IS supplied)
findings.body: The auto-generated warning at the top says: "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." But the migration itself uses `DEFAULT NOW()`, which is exactly the safe-handling approach that contradicts the warning. Either delete the stale warning block or rewrite it to reflect that a default was added (e.g., "Added required column `updatedAt` with a default of `NOW()` so existing rows are populated"). As shipped, the comment misrepresents the migration and would mislead a reviewer auditing why the migration is safe on a non-empty table.
